adaptations.withheld: sacred or restricted dance: no teaching adaptations

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Head dancer manipulates internal strings for eyes/ears; tail dancer holds the waist of the lead.
movement_profile.footwork: Intricate, feline steps in Hok San style; powerful, stable steps in Fut San.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Linear or circular paths through streets or across elevated platforms.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: The tail dancer must bend deeply to form the lion's back.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Frequent use of high-level lifts and jumps between platforms.
movement_profile.partnering: Tight synchronization between head and tail dancers is essential for a unified animal appearance.
movement_profile.posture: Low, grounded martial arts stances (Ma Bu).

signature_moves.description: Plucking the greens; the lion 'eats' lettuce to bring luck.
signature_moves.name: Choy Chang

signature_moves.description: Acrobatic leaps between high metal poles.
signature_moves.name: Jong jumping

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Burst-like; sudden explosive movements followed by cautious stillness.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid breaking the 'animal' illusion by showing the dancers' faces or losing synchronization between head and tail.

music_profile.musical_form: Sectional, following the narrative of the lion's journey
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Syncopated drum strikes following the lion's blinks and jumps
music_profile.sound_description: A loud, percussive wall of sound dominated by a large barrel drum, punctuated by the metallic crash of cymbals and gongs that mirror the lion's every blink and pounce.

basic_steps: Head shaking and ear twitching via internal pull-strings
teaching.level_notes: Only advanced martial arts students are traditionally allowed to perform the head in the Fut San style.
teaching.rhythm: Vigorous, syncopated percussion following the lion's emotional state.
